harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux. Demonstrated failover: stopped node1's postgres, promoted node2 to writable primary with zero committed-data loss, repointed node3 to follow node2, then rejoined node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Finally executed the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol on all three nodes, proving boot-identity change (boot_id) and post-reboot recovery of postgres role, replication streaming, and cluster data on each.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql16 on node1, node2, node3 via apk
Initialized primary DB on node1 with wal_level=replica, configured pg_hba.conf for replication
Started postgresql on node1, created replicator role with generated password (secret_env only)
Created appdb/ledger table with baseline committed rows on node1
pg_basebackup'd node2 and node3 from node1 with -R (standby.signal + primary_conninfo)
Started postgresql on node2/node3, verified streaming replication and data presence
Inserted a pre-failover committed row, confirmed replay on node2
Stopped postgresql on node1 to simulate primary loss
Promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote; verified writable and no data loss; inserted post-failover row
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2, restarted, confirmed streaming from new primary
Rebuilt node1 via pg_basebackup from node2 and started it as a standby; confirmed data intact and streaming to node2
Enabled postgresql in default runlevel (rc-update add) on all three nodes for reboot persistence
Sequentially rebooted node1, node2 (primary), then node3 one at a time using nohup-backgrounded reboot, polling boot_id and post-recovery health each time
Verified after each reboot: boot_id changed, postgresql auto-started, correct primary/standby role, replication streaming, and all ledger rows present

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established: node1 primary, node2+node3 standbys
evidence.summary: node1 initialized and started as primary with wal_level=replica; node2 and node3 base-backed up from node1 and started as standbys; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both walreceivers streaming; both standbys show pg_is_in_recovery=t with baseline data replicated

evidence.requirement: Failover: standby takes over as writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Committed row 'pre-failover-committed' replicated to node2 before primary loss; node1 postgres stopped (primary lost); node2 promoted via pg_ctl promote, pg_is_in_recovery=false; node2 accepted new write 'post-failover-on-node2' while retaining all prior committed rows including the pre-failover one

evidence.requirement: Other standby and recovered former primary follow the new primary
evidence.summary: node3 repointed primary_conninfo to node2 and confirmed streaming from it with post-failover data; node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2, started as standby, pg_is_in_recovery=true, all data intact; node2's pg_stat_replication shows both node1 and node3 streaming

Baseline boot_id e7e1795a captured with healthy standby state; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to cb7f5583 proving restart; postgresql auto-started as standby, pg_is_in_recovery=true, all 4 ledger rows present, node2 shows node1 streaming again

Baseline boot_id cb4a7f60 captured with healthy primary state (4 rows); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 9437928c proving restart; postgresql auto-started as primary, pg_is_in_recovery=false, all data intact, both node1 and node3 walreceivers reconnected and streaming

Baseline boot_id ec307870 captured with healthy standby state (4 rows); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to b42bc24f proving restart; postgresql auto-started as standby, pg_is_in_recovery=true, all data intact, node2 confirms node3 streaming again
